title: SS2 Science Practicals
summary: Hands-on practicals for senior secondary Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, done in virtual labs: find a hidden resistance with Ohm's law, titrate an acid of unknown strength, and find the equation of a straight line. Each topic has a short reading, a lab with your own numbers, and a quiz.
outcomes: Use an ammeter and a voltmeter correctly and apply V = IR to find an unknown resistance
Carry out an acid–base titration, obtain concordant titres and calculate a concentration
Find the gradient and intercept of a straight line and use y = mx + c
Record readings in a table and check them for mistakes before drawing conclusions
prerequisites: Senior secondary Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics up to SS1, and a calculator. The labs work on a phone, but a tablet or computer gives you more room.

lessons.title: Lab: the hidden resistor
lessons.intro: Your resistor is sealed in a box. Record at least three readings, then work out its resistance. You need 70% to pass, and you can try again with new numbers as often as you like.

lessons.title: Current electricity quiz
lessons.intro: Five questions on Ohm's law and meters.

questions.prompt: How is an ammeter connected to measure the current through a resistor?
questions.explanation: The same current must flow through the ammeter and the resistor, so it goes in series.

questions.prompt: A resistor has 6.0 V across it and 0.30 A through it. What is its resistance?
Why is the voltmeter reading across the resistor a little less than the cell's setting?
options: Current is used up in the resistor
questions.explanation: Some of the voltage is 'lost' across the cell's own internal resistance, so less is left across the resistor.

questions.prompt: On a graph of current against voltage for a resistor obeying Ohm's law, the line is…
options: straight but cuts the current axis above zero
questions.explanation: Current is proportional to voltage, so the graph is a straight line through (0, 0).

lessons.title: Lab: how strong is the acid?
lessons.intro: Do a rough run first, then accurate runs adding one drop at a time near the end point. Record your titres as you go.

lessons.title: Titration quiz
lessons.intro: Five questions on titration technique and calculations.

questions.prompt: Phenolphthalein in the flask turns from colourless to pink when…
questions.explanation: Phenolphthalein is colourless in acid and pink in alkali, so pink appears once alkali is in excess.

questions.prompt: Initial burette reading 1.10 cm³, final reading 23.45 cm³. What is the titre?

questions.explanation: Concordant titres agree within 0.20 cm³. 21.30 and 21.40 differ by 0.10 cm³.

questions.prompt: 22.00 cm³ of 0.100 mol/dm³ NaOH neutralises 25.0 cm³ of HCl. What is the HCl concentration?
Why do you add the alkali one drop at a time near the end point?
options: So you do not overshoot the end point
questions.explanation: A single drop can change the colour. Adding slowly lets you stop at the first permanent pink.

lessons.title: Lab: find the equation
lessons.intro: Work out the gradient and intercept from the plotted points first, then use the sliders to check that your line passes through all of them.

questions.prompt: What is the gradient of the line through (2, 3) and (6, 11)?
The line y = −3x + 4 crosses the y-axis at…
questions.explanation: At the y-axis x = 0, so y = 4.

questions.prompt: A line has gradient 0.5 and passes through (4, 1). What is c?
Which line goes down from left to right?
questions.explanation: A negative gradient means y decreases as x increases.
